grades.reason: Discusses symbolic-link race vulnerabilities, not reading files after unlink.

grades.quote: demonstrate a program continuing to make use of an open file after all names for that file have been removed. You can remove the names using `rm` in a shell, rather than needing to write a program that uses `unlink` .
grades.reason: Directly addresses demonstrating continued access after unlink, but does not explain the underlying lifetime rules.

grades.quote: iput() doesn’t truncate a file immediately when the link count for the file drops to zero, because some process might still hold a reference to the inode in memory
grades.reason: Explains that an inode reference keeps the file available even after its link count reaches zero.

grades.quote: The unlink system call removes a name from the file system. The file’s inode and the disk space holding its content are only freed when the file’s link count is zero and no file descriptors refer to it.
grades.reason: Directly explains why an open descriptor allows continued reading after unlink removes the file’s name.
